item.text: {"case_id":"SHC008","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C18","C04","C08"],"selected_candidate_label":"C18","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C18 is a compelling direct template because it addresses the identical distinctive problem—wrongful detention of U.S. nationals abroad—and supplies concrete machinery reused by the child: State Department identification or designation, sanctions under IEEPA, section 7031(c) designations, immigration restrictions coordinated with Homeland Security, and statutory definitions of wrongful detention and U.S. nationals. The child reorganizes that person-focused sanctions framework into a country-level designation-and-response regime, but the shared language, authorities, actors, and operative tools are too specific and extensive to be explained as broad topical similarity or routine boilerplate. C04 and C08 are the next strongest because they use a determination that a foreign country committed specified conduct, followed by a defined menu of country-level assistance, arms, and export restrictions and provisions governing termination, but their different WMD subject makes them weaker than C18.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The United States must strengthen efforts to protect U.S. nationals from wrongful detention abroad... using every tool available to curb this coercive tactic... and must hold such adversaries to account.","parent_excerpt":"The United States Government must redouble its efforts... to deter these practices and to secure the release of those held as hostages or wrongfully detained... [and] impose tangible consequences on those responsible for, or complicit in... wrongful detention of a United States national abroad.","explanation":"The purpose clauses share the same distinctive policy problem and the same deter-and-impose-consequences framing."},{"child_excerpt":"The Secretary of State may designate any foreign country the government of which directly engages in or provides support for the wrongful detention of a U.S. national","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of State shall publicly or privately designate or identify officials of foreign governments who are involved, directly or indirectly, in wrongful detentions","explanation":"The child adapts C18's State-led identification mechanism from responsible foreign officials to responsible foreign countries."},{"child_excerpt":"including: (a) imposing sanctions available under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act...; (b) making designations under section 7031(c)...; (c) applying inadmissibility available under the Immigration and Nationality Act... coordinating with the Department of Homeland Security","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of State shall... designate or identify officials... including section 7031(c)... All property and interests in property... are blocked... [and] the entry of such persons... is hereby suspended... The Secretary of State [and] Secretary of Homeland Security shall implement","explanation":"The child reuses C18's distinctive package of IEEPA sanctions, section 7031(c) accountability, and coordinated visa or entry restrictions."},{"child_excerpt":"the term \"wrongful detention\" refers to the detention of a U.S. national the Secretary of State has determined to be unlawful or wrongful pursuant to the Levinson Act; and... \"U.S. national\" has the same meaning as \"United States national\" given in 22 U.S.C. 1741e(2).","parent_excerpt":"the term \"United States national\" means... a \"national of the United States\"... or... a lawful permanent resident with significant ties...; and... the term \"wrongful detention\" means a detention that the Secretary of State has determined to be wrongful consistent with section 302(a) of the Levinson Act.","explanation":"Both orders formally define the same core concepts through State Department determinations and the Levinson Act, strongly indicating reuse of subject-specific drafting material."}]}
